metadata.title: Proof of the High Girth Existence Conjecture via Refined Absorption

nodes.name: Steiner system / Design
nodes.statement: A \emph{Steiner system} with parameters $(n,q,r)$ is a set $S$ of $q$-subsets of an $n$-set $X$ such that every $r$-subset of $X$ belongs to exactly one element of $S$. A \emph{design} with parameters $(n,q,r,\lambda)$ replaces 'exactly one' with 'exactly $\lambda$'.

nodes.name: Existence Conjecture
nodes.statement: Let $q > r \ge 2$ and $\lambda \geq 1$ be integers. If $n$ is sufficiently large and $\binom{q-i}{r-i} \mid \lambda \binom{n-i}{r-i}$ for all $0 \le i \le r-1$, then there exists a design with parameters $(n,q,r,\lambda)$.
conclusions: there exists a design with parameters $(n,q,r,\lambda)$

nodes.name: Existence Theorem (Keevash)
nodes.statement: The Existence Conjecture is true.
conclusions: the Existence Conjecture (designs with parameters $(n,q,r,\lambda)$ exist when divisibility holds and $n$ is large) is true

nodes.name: Configuration / Girth of partial Steiner system
nodes.statement: In a partial $(n,q,r)$-Steiner system, a $(j,i)$-configuration is a set of $i$ $q$-element subsets spanning at most $j$ vertices. The \emph{girth} is the smallest integer $g \geq 2$ such that the system has a $((q-r)g+r,g)$-configuration.

nodes.name: Existence of High Girth Steiner Triple Systems (Erdos)
nodes.statement: For every integer $g \geq 2$, there exists $n_g$ such that for all $n \geq n_g$ where $n \equiv 1, 3 \bmod 6$, there exists an $(n,3,2)$-Steiner system with girth at least $g$.
conclusions: there exists an $(n,3,2)$-Steiner system with girth at least $g$

nodes.name: Resolution of Erdos Conjecture (Kwan-Sah-Sawhney-Simkin)
nodes.statement: Erdos' Conjecture (Conjecture~\ref{conj:Erdos}) is true.
conclusions: high girth Steiner triple systems exist for all sufficiently large admissible $n$

nodes.name: Existence of High Girth Designs
nodes.statement: For all integers $q > r \geq 2$ and every integer $g \ge 2$, there exists $n_0$ such that for all $n \ge n_0$ where $\binom{q-i}{r-i} \mid \binom{n-i}{r-i}$ for all $0 \le i \le r-1$, there exists an $(n,q,r)$-Steiner system with girth at least $g$.
conclusions: there exists an $(n,q,r)$-Steiner system with girth at least $g$

nodes.name: Existence of High Girth Designs
nodes.statement: Conjecture~\ref{conj:HighGirthAllUniformities} (Existence of High Girth Designs) is true.
conclusions: the Existence of High Girth Designs Conjecture holds for all $q > r \ge 2$ and $g \ge 2$

nodes.name: Why $\lambda=1$ only
nodes.statement: For $\lambda \ge 2$, a design with parameters $(n,q,r,\lambda)$ necessarily contains a $((q-r)\cdot 2 + r, 2)$-configuration and hence has girth $2$, so the conjectures need amendment in that regime.

nodes.name: Absorber
nodes.statement: Let $L$ be a $K_q^r$-divisible hypergraph. A hypergraph $A$ is a \emph{$K_q^r$-absorber} for $L$ if $V(L) \subseteq V(A)$ is independent in $A$ and both $A$ and $A \cup L$ admit $K_q^r$ decompositions.

nodes.name: Omni-Absorber
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a hypergraph. A hypergraph $A$ is a \emph{$K_q^r$-omni-absorber} for $X$ with decomposition family $\mathcal{H}$ and decomposition function $\mathcal{Q}_A$ if $V(X)=V(A)$, $X$ and $A$ are edge-disjoint, $|H \cap X| \le 1$ for all $H \in \mathcal{H}$, and for every $K_q^r$-divisible $L \subseteq X$, $\mathcal{Q}_A(L) \subseteq \mathcal{H}$ are pairwise edge-disjoint with $\bigcup \mathcal{Q}_A(L) = L \cup A$.

nodes.name: Refined Omni-Absorber
nodes.statement: A $K_q^r$-omni-absorber $A$ for $X$ with decomposition family $\mathcal{H}$ is \emph{$C$-refined} if $|\{H \in \mathcal{H} : e \in E(H)\}| \le C$ for every edge $e \in X \cup A$.

nodes.name: Refined Omni-Absorber Theorem
nodes.statement: For all integers $q > r \ge 1$, there exist $C \ge 1$ and $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ such that: if $G$ is $r$-uniform on $n$ vertices with $\delta(G) \ge (1-\varepsilon)n$ and $X \subseteq G$ has $\Delta(X) \le n/C$, then with $\Delta := \max\{\Delta(X), n^{1-1/r} \log n\}$ there exists a $C$-refined $K_q^r$-omni-absorber $A \subseteq G$ for $X$ with $\Delta(A) \le C \cdot \Delta$.
conclusions: there exists a $C$-refined $K_q^r$-omni-absorber $A \subseteq G$ for $X$ with $\Delta(A) \le C \cdot \Delta$

nodes.name: Collective girth of omni-absorber
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an $r$-uniform hypergraph. A $K_q^r$-omni-absorber $A$ for $X$ with decomposition function $\mathcal{Q}_A$ has \emph{collective girth at least $g$} if for every $K_q^r$-divisible subgraph $L$ of $X$, $\mathcal{Q}_A(L)$ has girth at least $g$.

nodes.name: Booster
nodes.statement: A \emph{$K_q^r$-booster} is an $r$-uniform hypergraph $B$ along with two $K_q^r$ decompositions $\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2$ of $B$ such that $\mathcal{B}_1 \cap \mathcal{B}_2 = \emptyset$.

nodes.name: Rooted Booster
nodes.statement: A \emph{rooted $K_q^r$-booster} rooted at $S \cong K_q^r$ is an $r$-uniform hypergraph $B$ edge-disjoint from $S$ along with two disjoint $K_q^r$ packings $\mathcal{B}_{\rm off}, \mathcal{B}_{\rm on}$ where $\mathcal{B}_{\rm off}$ is a $K_q^r$-decomposition of $B$ and $\mathcal{B}_{\rm on}$ is a $K_q^r$-decomposition of $B \cup S$ with $S \notin \mathcal{B}_{\rm on}$.

nodes.name: Rooted Girth
nodes.statement: For a $K_q^r$-packing $\mathcal{B}$ of a graph $G$ and $S \subseteq V(G)$, the \emph{rooted girth} of $\mathcal{B}$ at $S$ is the smallest integer $g \ge 1$ such that there exists $\mathcal{B}' \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ with $|\mathcal{B}'|=g$ and $|V(\bigcup \mathcal{B}') \setminus S| < (q-r) \cdot g$.

nodes.name: High Rooted Girth Booster Theorem
nodes.statement: Let $q > r \ge 2$ and $g \ge 1$ be integers. If Theorem~\ref{thm:HighCogirthBooster} holds for $r' := r-1$, then there exists a rooted $K_q^r$-booster $B$ with rooted girth at least $g$.
conclusions: there exists a rooted $K_q^r$-booster $B$ with rooted girth at least $g$

nodes.name: Design Hypergraph
nodes.statement: If $G$ is a hypergraph and $F$ is a hypergraph, the \emph{$F$-design hypergraph of $G$}, ${\rm Design}_F(G)$, is the hypergraph $\mathcal{D}$ with $V(\mathcal{D}) := E(G)$ and $E(\mathcal{D}) := \{S \subseteq E(G) : S \text{ isomorphic to } F\}$.

nodes.name: Omni-Booster
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be $r$-uniform and $A$ a $K_q^r$-omni-absorber for $X$. An $r$-uniform hypergraph $B$ is a \emph{$K_q^r$-omni-booster} for $A$ and $X$ if $B$ is edge-disjoint from $A \cup X$ and is the edge-disjoint union of $\mathcal{B} = (B_H : H \in \mathcal{H})$ where each $B_H$ is a rooted $K_q^r$-booster rooted at $H$. The matching set $\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{B})$ collects $H$-indexed selections of on/off decompositions; $B$ has \emph{collective girth at least $g$} if every $M \in \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{B})$ has girth at least $g$.

nodes.name: Reserve Design Hypergraph
nodes.statement: If $G$ is a hypergraph and $A, B \subseteq E(G)$ disjoint, the \emph{$F$-design reserve hypergraph} ${\rm Reserve}_F(G,A,B)$ is the bipartite hypergraph $\mathcal{D} = (A,B)$ with $V(\mathcal{D}) = A \cup B$ and $E(\mathcal{D}) := \{S \subseteq A \cup B : S \cong F, |S \cap A|=1\}$.

nodes.name: Random Reserve Lemma
nodes.statement: For all $q > r \ge 1$, there exists $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ such that: if $G$ is $r$-uniform with $\delta(G) \ge (1-\varepsilon) v(G)$ and $v(G)^{-\varepsilon} \le p \le 1$ and $v(G) \ge 1/\varepsilon$, then there exists a spanning $X \subseteq G$ with $\Delta(X) \le 2p \cdot v(G)$ and for all $e \in G \setminus X$, at least $\varepsilon \cdot p^{\binom{q}{r}-1} \cdot v(G)^{q-r}$ $K_q^r$'s in $X \cup \{e\}$ contain $e$.
conclusions: there exists spanning $X \subseteq G$ with $\Delta(X) \le 2p \cdot v(G)$ and the stated $K_q^r$-count property

nodes.name: Boost Lemma (regularity boosting)
nodes.statement: For all $q > r \ge 1$ and reals $d, \xi, \varepsilon > 0$ with $d \ge \xi \ge 2(2\sqrt{e})^r \varepsilon$, there exists $n_0$ such that for $n \ge n_0$: if $J$ is $r$-uniform on $n$ vertices and $\mathcal{J} \subseteq {\rm Design}_{K_q^r}(J)$ is $(d \pm \varepsilon) n^{q-r}$-regular and edges of $J$ have $\xi n^q$ many extending $q$-subsets in $\mathcal{J}$, then there exists $H \subseteq \mathcal{J}$ with $d_H(v) = (1 \pm n^{-(q-r)/3}) \cdot \frac{d}{2} n^{q-r}$ for all $v \in V(H)$.
conclusions: a regular subhypergraph $H$ of $\mathcal{J}$ with $d_H(v) = (1 \pm n^{-(q-r)/3}) (d/2) n^{q-r}$ exists

nodes.name: $A$-perfect matching
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a hypergraph and $A \subseteq V(G)$. A matching of $G$ is \emph{$A$-perfect} if every vertex of $A$ is in an edge of the matching.

nodes.name: Bipartite Hypergraph
nodes.statement: A hypergraph $G = (A, B)$ is \emph{bipartite with parts $A, B$} if $V(G) = A \cup B$ and every edge contains exactly one vertex from $A$.

nodes.name: Configuration Hypergraph
nodes.statement: A hypergraph $H$ is a \emph{configuration hypergraph} for $G$ if $E(G) \subseteq V(H)$ and every edge $e$ of $H$ has $|e| \ge 2$ and $e \cap E(G)$ is a matching of $G$. A matching of $G$ is \emph{$H$-avoiding} if it spans no edge of $H$.

nodes.name: Treasury
nodes.statement: An \emph{$(r,g)$-treasury} is a tuple $T = (G_1, G_2, H)$ where $G_1$ is $r$-uniform, $G_2 = (A,B)$ is $r$-bounded bipartite with $V(G_1) \cap V(G_2) = A$, and $H$ is a $g$-bounded configuration hypergraph of $G_1 \cup G_2$. A \emph{perfect matching} is an $H$-avoiding $A$-perfect matching of $G_1 \cup G_2$. $T$ is \emph{$(D,\sigma,\beta,\alpha)$-regular} if quasi-regularity, reserve degrees, weighted-degree bounds and codegree bounds (specified in paper) hold.

nodes.name: Forbidden Submatchings with Reserves
nodes.statement: For all $r, g \ge 2$ and $\beta \in (0,1)$, there exist $D_\beta \ge 0$ and $\alpha > 0$ such that for all $D \ge D_\beta$: if $T$ is an $(r,g)$-treasury that is $(D, D^{1-\beta}, \beta, \alpha)$-regular, then there exists a perfect matching of $T$.
conclusions: there exists a perfect matching of $T$

nodes.name: Erdos configuration
nodes.statement: An $(i(q-r)+r, i)$ \emph{Erdos-configuration} of an $r$-graph $G$ is an $(i(q-r)+r, i)$-configuration containing no $(i'(q-r)+r, i')$-configuration for any $2 \le i' < i$.

nodes.name: Girth Configuration Hypergraph
nodes.statement: Given $G$ $r$-uniform and $\mathcal{D} = {\rm Design}_{K_q^r}(G)$, the \emph{girth-$g$ $K_q^r$-configuration hypergraph} ${\rm Girth}_{K_q^r}^g(G)$ is the configuration hypergraph $H$ of $\mathcal{D}$ with $V(H) = E(\mathcal{D})$ and $E(H) = \{S \subseteq E(\mathcal{D}): S \text{ is an } (i(q-r)+r,i) \text{ Erdos-configuration of } G \text{ for some } 3 \le i \le g\}$.

nodes.name: Girth-$g$ design treasury
nodes.statement: ${\rm Treasury}_q^g(G, G', X) := ({\rm Design}_{K_q^r}(G' \setminus X), {\rm Reserve}_{K_q^r}(G, G' \setminus X, X), {\rm Girth}_{K_q^r}^g(G))$.

nodes.name: Turan-type density
nodes.statement: For all $q > r \ge 1$ and $\alpha > 0$, there exist $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ and $n_0 \ge 1$ such that for $n \ge n_0$: if $G$ is $r$-uniform on $n$ vertices with $\delta(G) \ge (1-\varepsilon)n$, then for every edge $e$ of $G$ there exist at least $(1-\alpha) \binom{n}{q-r}$ $K_q^r$'s containing $e$.
conclusions: every edge $e$ of $G$ is in at least $(1-\alpha) \binom{n}{q-r}$ $K_q^r$'s

nodes.name: Random Reserve Treasury Regularity
nodes.statement: For all $q > r \ge 1$, $g \ge 3$ and $\alpha > 0$, there exist $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ and $n_0$ such that: if $G$ is $r$-uniform on $n \ge n_0$ vertices with $\delta(G) \ge (1-\varepsilon) n$, then there exists spanning $X \subseteq G$ with $\Delta(X) \le 2 n^{1-\varepsilon}$ such that ${\rm Treasury}_q^g(G, G, X)$ is $(\binom{n}{q-r}, \alpha \binom{n}{q-r}, \frac{1}{2g(q-r)}, \alpha)$-regular.
conclusions: there exists $X$ with $\Delta(X) \le 2n^{1-\varepsilon}$ such that the girth-$g$ design treasury of $G$ is $(\binom{n}{q-r}, \alpha \binom{n}{q-r}, \frac{1}{2g(q-r)}, \alpha)$-regular

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma RandomXTreasury
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:RandomX} with $p = n^{-\varepsilon}$ and verify each treasury parameter (degrees, codegrees, weighted degrees) using Proposition~\ref{prop:Turan} and counting arguments.

nodes.name: Common projection of treasury by matching family
nodes.statement: For treasury $T = (G_1, G_2, H)$ and family $\mathcal{M} = \{M_1, \ldots, M_k\}$ of vertex subsets each of which intersects $G_1 \cup G_2$ in a matching, the \emph{common projection} $T \perp \mathcal{M}$ is a treasury $T' = (G_1', G_2', H')$ where $V(H')$ removes singletons completed by some $M_i$ and $E(H')$ records leftover sub-configurations after projecting away matchings.

nodes.name: Girth-$g$ projection treasury of an omni-absorber
nodes.statement: For $A \subseteq G$ a $K_q^r$-omni-absorber of $X$ with decomposition function $\mathcal{Q}_A$, ${\rm Proj}_g(A, G, X) := {\rm Treasury}_q^g(G, G \setminus A, X) \perp \mathcal{M}(A)$ where $\mathcal{M}(A) = \{\mathcal{Q}_A(L) : L \subseteq X \text{ is } K_q^r\text{-divisible}\}$.

nodes.name: Find Steiner System from Projection Matching
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be $K_q^r$-divisible $r$-uniform, $X \subseteq G$, and $A \subseteq G$ a $K_q^r$-omni-absorber for $X$ of collective girth at least $g$. If a perfect matching of ${\rm Proj}_g(A, G, X)$ exists, then there exists a $K_q^r$-decomposition of $G$ of girth at least $g$.
assumptions: $A \subseteq G$ is $K_q^r$-omni-absorber for $X$ of collective girth at least $g$
a perfect matching of ${\rm Proj}_g(A,G,X)$ exists
conclusions: there exists a $K_q^r$-decomposition of $G$ of girth at least $g$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition FindSteiner
nodes.statement: Take a perfect matching $M$ of the projected treasury, set $L := X \setminus \bigcup M$, observe $L$ is $K_q^r$-divisible, then $M \cup \mathcal{Q}_A(L)$ is a high-girth decomposition.

nodes.name: Subtreasury
nodes.statement: $(G_1', G_2', H')$ is a \emph{subtreasury} of $(G_1, G_2, H)$ if $G_i'$ is a spanning subgraph of $G_i$ for each $i$ and $H[E(G_1') \cup E(G_2')]$ is a subgraph of $H'$.

nodes.name: Subtreasury preserves perfect matchings
nodes.statement: If $T'$ is a subtreasury of $T$ and $M$ is a perfect matching of $T'$, then $M$ is a perfect matching of $T$.
conclusions: $M$ is a perfect matching of $T$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition SubTreasury
nodes.statement: By definition $M$ is $H'$-avoiding $A$-perfect matching of $G_1' \cup G_2'$; spanning property gives $A = V(G_1) \cap V(G_2)$, and $H'$-avoidance lifts to $H$-avoidance.

nodes.name: Sub-projection treasury monotonicity
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{M}' \supseteq \mathcal{M}$, then $T \perp \mathcal{M}'$ is a subtreasury of $T \perp \mathcal{M}$.
conclusions: $T \perp \mathcal{M}'$ is a subtreasury of $T \perp \mathcal{M}$

nodes.name: High Girth Omni-Absorber Theorem
nodes.statement: For all $q > r \ge 1$, $g \ge 3$, $\alpha \in (0, \tfrac{1}{2(q-r)})$, there exist $a, n_0$ such that for $n \ge n_0$: assuming Theorem~\ref{thm:HighCogirthBooster} for $r-1$, if $X \subseteq K_n^r$ has $\Delta(X) \le n / \log^{ga} n$ and ${\rm Treasury}_q^g(K_n^r, K_n^r, X)$ is $(\binom{n}{q-r}, \alpha \binom{n}{q-r}, \frac{1}{2g(q-r)}, \alpha)$-regular, then a $K_q^r$-omni-absorber $A$ for $X$ exists with $\Delta(A) \le a \Delta \log^a \Delta$ and collective girth $\ge g$ together with a regular subtreasury of ${\rm Proj}_g(A, K_n^r, X)$.
assumptions: $X$ spanning subgraph of $K_n^r$ with $\Delta(X) \le n/\log^{ga} n$
conclusions: there exists a $K_q^r$-omni-absorber $A$ for $X$ with $\Delta(A) \le a \Delta \log^a \Delta$, collective girth at least $g$, and a $(\binom{n}{q-r}, 3\alpha \binom{n}{q-r}, \frac{1}{4g(q-r)}, 2\alpha)$-regular subtreasury of ${\rm Proj}_g(A, K_n^r, X)$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem HighGirthSteiner
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:RandomXTreasury} to obtain reserve $X$ and regular treasury, then apply Theorem~\ref{thm:HighGirthAbsorber} to obtain a high-girth omni-absorber $A$ with regular projection subtreasury, regularity-boost via Lemma~\ref{lem:RegBoost}, apply Theorem~\ref{thm:ForbiddenSubmatchingReserves} for a perfect matching, and lift to a high-girth $K_q^r$-decomposition via Proposition~\ref{prop:FindSteiner}.

nodes.name: Pick parameters $r', \beta', \alpha', \alpha, \varepsilon$
nodes.statement: Let $r' := \binom{q}{r}$, $\beta' := \frac{1}{8g(q-r)}$, $\alpha'$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:ForbiddenSubmatchingReserves} for $r', g, \beta'$, and $\alpha$ small enough so $\alpha \le \alpha'/2^{g+1}$ and $\alpha < \frac{1}{2(q-r)}$.

nodes.name: Reserve $X$ via random selection
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:RandomXTreasury}, obtain a spanning $X \subseteq K_n^r$ with $\Delta(X) \le 2 n^{1-\varepsilon}$ such that ${\rm Treasury}_q^g(K_n^r, K_n^r, X)$ is regular with the appropriate parameters.

nodes.name: Construct high-girth omni-absorber $A$ and subtreasury $T$
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{thm:HighGirthAbsorber} for $q, r, g, \alpha$, obtain a $K_q^r$-omni-absorber $A$ with $\Delta(A) \le a \Delta \log^a \Delta$ and collective girth $\ge g$, plus a regular subtreasury $T = (G_1, G_2, H)$ of ${\rm Proj}_g(A, K_n^r, X)$.

nodes.name: Apply Boost Lemma to $J = K_n^r \setminus (X \cup A)$
nodes.statement: Set $d = 1/(q-r)!$, $\xi = 1/(2(q-r)!)$, $\varepsilon' = 4\alpha$, $\mathcal{J} = G_1$. Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:RegBoost} to find subhypergraph $G_1' \subseteq \mathcal{J}$ with regular degrees of order $\frac{d}{2} n^{q-r}$.

nodes.name: Verify subtreasury $T'$ is $(D', \sigma', \beta', \alpha')$-regular
nodes.statement: Form $T' = (G_1', G_2, H[G_1' \cup G_2])$ and verify each treasury parameter (degrees of $G_1', G_2$, codegrees, $\Delta_i(H')$) using $T$'s regularity, $G_1' \subseteq G_1$, $D' \ge D/2$, and $\alpha' \ge 2^{g+1}\alpha$.

nodes.name: Apply Forbidden Submatchings with Reserves and conclude
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{thm:ForbiddenSubmatchingReserves}, $T'$ has a perfect matching $M$. Lifting via Propositions~\ref{prop:SubTreasury} and~\ref{prop:FindSteiner}, $K_n^r$ has a $K_q^r$-decomposition of girth $\ge g$.

nodes.name: Cogirth
nodes.statement: For $K_q^r$-packings $\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2$ of $G$, the \emph{cogirth} is the smallest $g \ge 2$ for which $\mathcal{B}_1 \cup \mathcal{B}_2$ contains a $(g(q-r)+r-1, g)$-configuration. For a $K_q^r$-booster $B$ with decompositions $\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2$, the cogirth is the minimum of the girths of $\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2$ and the cogirth of the pair.

nodes.name: High Cogirth Booster Theorem
nodes.statement: Let $q > r \ge 1$ and $g \ge 2$ be integers. There exists a $K_q^r$-booster $B$ with cogirth at least $g$.
conclusions: there exists a $K_q^r$-booster $B$ with cogirth at least $g$

nodes.name: Existence of High Cogirth Designs
nodes.statement: For all $q > r \ge 1$ and every $g \ge 2$, there exists $n_0$ such that for all admissible $n \ge n_0$, there exist two $(n, q, r)$-Steiner systems both with girth at least $g$ and cogirth at least $g$.
conclusions: there exist two $(n,q,r)$-Steiner systems both of girth at least $g$ and pairwise cogirth at least $g$

nodes.name: First Construction (almost-rooted booster)
nodes.statement: Let $q \ge r \ge 2$ and $g \ge 3$. If Theorem~\ref{thm:HighCogirthBooster} holds for $r' = r-1$, then there exists a $K_q^r$-booster $B$ with disjoint $K_q^r$-decompositions $\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2$ and cliques $S \in \mathcal{B}_1$, $S' \in \mathcal{B}_2$ with $|S \cap S'| = q-1$ such that (1) $\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2$ have girth $\ge g$ and (2) $\mathcal{B}_2 \setminus \{S'\}$ has rooted girth at $V(S) \cup V(S')$ at least $g$.
conclusions: there exists a $K_q^r$-booster $B$ with disjoint decompositions $\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2$ and cliques $S, S'$ as described, with girth and rooted girth properties (1)-(2) holding

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma HighGirthBoost
nodes.statement: Construct $B$ from a high-girth-and-cogirth $K_{q-1}^{r-1}$-booster $B'$ by adding two new vertices $v_1, v_2$ and lifting each clique $Q \in \mathcal{B}_1' \cup \mathcal{B}_2'$ to $\phi_i(Q)$.

nodes.name: Construct $B$ via gluing
nodes.statement: Let $V(B) = V(B') \cup \{v_1, v_2\}$ and $E(B) = \{\{v_i\} \cup e : e \in E(B'), i \in [2]\} \cup \bigcup_{Q \in \mathcal{B}_1' \cup \mathcal{B}_2'} \binom{Q}{r}$.

nodes.name: Define $\phi_i$ and decompositions $\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2$
nodes.statement: Define $\phi_i(Q) = \{\{v_i\} \cup e : e \in Q\} \cup \binom{Q}{r}$ and form $\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2$ by combining $\phi_1, \phi_2$ images of $\mathcal{B}_1', \mathcal{B}_2'$ in crossed fashion.

nodes.name: Claim girth at least $g+1$ for $\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2$
nodes.statement: Case-split on $|V(T) \cap \{v_1, v_2\}| \in \{1, 2\}$ and use girth/cogirth of $\mathcal{B}_1', \mathcal{B}_2'$ to lower-bound $|V(T)|$.

nodes.name: Pick $S, S'$ and prove rooted girth claim
nodes.statement: Choose $S = \phi_1(Q)$ and $S' = \phi_2(Q)$ for some $Q \in \mathcal{B}_1'$; show $\mathcal{B}_2 \setminus \{S'\}$ has rooted girth $\ge g$ at $V(S) \cup V(S')$ by extending $\mathcal{T} \to \mathcal{T} \cup \{S'\}$ and applying the prior girth claim.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem HighRootedGirthBooster (iterating construction)
nodes.statement: Choose $B$ minimizing $i = |S \cap S'|$ subject to the conditions of Lemma~\ref{lem:HighGirthBoost}. If $i = 0$, the construction yields rooted girth $\ge g$ directly; if $i > 0$, glue another booster $B'$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:HighGirthBoost} along $S'$ to obtain $B''$ with strictly smaller intersection, contradicting minimality.

nodes.name: Choose minimal-$i$ booster $B$
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:HighGirthBoost}, choose $B$, $\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2$, $S \in \mathcal{B}_1$, $S' \in \mathcal{B}_2$ with $|S \cap S'| = i$ minimum, satisfying conditions (1)-(2).

nodes.name: Base case $i = 0$
nodes.statement: If $i = 0$, every $\mathcal{T} \subseteq \mathcal{B}_2$ either avoids $S'$ (use (2)) or contains it (use $|V(S') \setminus V(S)| = q$ + (2)) to conclude $|V(T) \setminus V(S)| \ge (q-r) j$.

nodes.name: Inductive step $i > 0$: glue booster $B'$
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:HighGirthBoost} to obtain a second booster $B'$ rooted at $S'$ with $|S' \cap S''| = r-1$, glue $B'' = B \cup B'$ with $\mathcal{B}_1'' = \mathcal{B}_1 \cup (\mathcal{B}_1' \setminus \{S'\})$, $\mathcal{B}_2'' = (\mathcal{B}_2 \setminus \{S'\}) \cup \mathcal{B}_2'$.

nodes.name: Verify (1) and (2) for $B''$, $S, S''$
nodes.statement: Show $\mathcal{B}_1'', \mathcal{B}_2''$ have girth $\ge g$ (claim 1) and $\mathcal{B}_2'' \setminus \{S''\}$ has rooted girth at $V(S) \cup V(S'')$ $\ge g$ (claim 2) via case-decomposition of $\mathcal{T}''$ along $\mathcal{B}, \mathcal{B}'$.

nodes.name: Contradict minimality
nodes.statement: Since $|S \cap S''| < |S \cap S'| = i$, the existence of $B''$ contradicts the minimal choice of $B$, completing the induction.

nodes.name: Sponge
nodes.statement: A triple $\mathcal{S} = (G, A, X)$ is a \emph{$K_q^r$-sponge} if $G$ is $r$-uniform, $X \subseteq G$, and $A \subseteq G \setminus X$ is a $K_q^r$-omni-absorber for $X$. $\mathcal{S}$ is \emph{$(\alpha, g)$-regular}, \emph{$a$-bounded}, or \emph{$C$-refined} as defined via the corresponding regularity, $\Delta(X) \le v(G)/\log^a v(G)$, or $A$ being $C$-refined with $\Delta(A)$-bound.

nodes.name: Canonical Omni-Absorber from Omni-Booster
nodes.statement: Let $(G, A, X, \mathcal{H})$ be a $K_q^r$-sponge with decomposition function $\mathcal{Q}_A$. If $B$ is a $K_q^r$-omni-booster for $A$ and $X$ with booster family $\mathcal{B}$, then $A \cup B$ is a $K_q^r$-omni-absorber for $X$ with canonical decomposition function $\mathcal{Q}_{A \cup B}(L) = \bigcup_{H \in \mathcal{Q}_A(L)} (\mathcal{B}_H)_{\rm on} \cup \bigcup_{H \in \mathcal{H} \setminus \mathcal{Q}_A(L)} (\mathcal{B}_H)_{\rm off}$.
assumptions: $B$ is a $K_q^r$-omni-booster for $A$ and $X$ with booster family $\mathcal{B}$
conclusions: $A \cup B$ is a $K_q^r$-omni-absorber for $X$ with the stated canonical decomposition function

nodes.name: Girth-$g$ projection treasury of an omni-booster
nodes.statement: ${\rm Proj}_g(B, A, G, X) := {\rm Treasury}_q^g(G, G \setminus (A \cup B), X) \perp \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{B})$.

nodes.name: Booster projection is a subtreasury of canonical-absorber projection
nodes.statement: ${\rm Proj}_g(B, A, G, X)$ is a subtreasury of ${\rm Proj}_g(A \cup B, G, X)$.
conclusions: ${\rm Proj}_g(B,A,G,X)$ is a subtreasury of ${\rm Proj}_g(A \cup B, G, X)$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition BoosterSubTreasury
nodes.statement: Note $\mathcal{M}(A \cup B) \subseteq \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{B})$ and apply Proposition~\ref{prop:SubProjTreasury}.

nodes.name: High Girth Omni-Booster Theorem
nodes.statement: For all $q > r \ge 1$, $C \ge 1$, $g \ge 3$ and $\alpha \in (0, \tfrac{1}{2(q-r)})$, there exist $a, n_0$ such that for $n \ge n_0$: assuming Theorem~\ref{thm:HighCogirthBooster} for $r-1$, if $(K_n^r, A, X)$ is an $(\alpha,g)$-regular $ga$-bounded $C$-refined $K_q^r$-sponge, then there exists a $K_q^r$-omni-booster $B$ for $A$ and $X$ with $\Delta(B) \le a \Delta \log^a \Delta$, collective girth $\ge g$, and a $(\binom{n}{q-r}, 3\alpha \binom{n}{q-r}, \frac{1}{4g(q-r)}, 2\alpha)$-regular subtreasury of ${\rm Proj}_g(B, A, K_n^r, X)$.
conclusions: a $K_q^r$-omni-booster $B$ for $A$ and $X$ exists with $\Delta(B) \le a \Delta \log^a \Delta$, collective girth at least $g$, and a regular subtreasury of ${\rm Proj}_g(B, A, K_n^r, X)$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem HighGirthAbsorber from HighGirthOmniBooster
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:Omni} to obtain a refined absorber $A_0$, then Theorem~\ref{thm:HighGirthOmniBooster} to add a booster $B$, set $A := A_0 \cup B$, and conclude via Propositions~\ref{prop:CanonicalBoost} and~\ref{prop:BoosterSubTreasury}.

nodes.name: Quantum Omni-Booster
nodes.statement: A \emph{quantum $K_q^r$-omni-booster} for $(G, A, X, \mathcal{H})$ is an $r$-uniform $B$ together with $\mathcal{B} = (\mathcal{B}_H : H \in \mathcal{H})$ where each $\mathcal{B}_H$ is a family of (not necessarily edge-disjoint) $K_q^r$-boosters rooted at $H$ in $G \setminus (X \cup A)$. The matching set, ${\rm Disjoint}(\mathcal{B}_H)$, and ${\rm HighGirth}_g(\mathcal{B}_H)$ are defined to capture viable selections.

nodes.name: Girth-$g$ projection treasury of a quantum omni-booster
nodes.statement: ${\rm Proj}_g(B, A, G, X) := {\rm Treasury}_q^g(G, G \setminus A, X) \perp \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{B})$.

nodes.name: Quantum to ordinary booster subtreasury
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{B}' = (B_H : H \in \mathcal{H})$ with $B_H \in \mathcal{B}_H$ pairwise edge-disjoint, then $B' = \bigcup B_H$ is a $K_q^r$-omni-booster for $A$ and ${\rm Proj}_g(B', A, G, X)$ is a subtreasury of ${\rm Proj}_g(B, A, G, X)$.
conclusions: $B' = \bigcup B_H$ is a $K_q^r$-omni-booster for $A$ and ${\rm Proj}_g(B', A, G, X)$ is a subtreasury of ${\rm Proj}_g(B, A, G, X)$

nodes.name: High Girth Quantum Omni-Booster Theorem
nodes.statement: For all $q > r \ge 1$, $C \ge 1$, $g \ge 3$ and $\alpha \in (0, \tfrac{1}{2(q-r)})$, there exist $a, n_0$ such that for $n \ge n_0$: assuming Theorem~\ref{thm:HighCogirthBooster} for $r-1$, if $(K_n^r, A, X, \mathcal{H})$ is an $(\alpha, g)$-regular $ga$-bounded $C$-refined sponge, then there exists a quantum $K_q^r$-omni-booster $B$ with (1) $\Delta(B) \le \Delta \log^a \Delta$ and ${\rm Disjoint}(\mathcal{B}_H) \cap {\rm HighGirth}_g(\mathcal{B}_H) \ne \emptyset$ for each $H$ and (2) ${\rm Proj}_g(B, A, K_n^r, X)$ is $(\binom{n}{q-r}, 2\alpha \binom{n}{q-r}, \frac{1}{4g(q-r)}, 2\alpha)$-regular.
conclusions: a quantum $K_q^r$-omni-booster $B$ exists with the stated bounded-degree, ${\rm Disjoint} \cap {\rm HighGirth}$, and projection-regularity properties (1)-(2)

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem HighGirthOmniBooster from Quantum theorem
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:HighGirthQuantumOmniBooster}, choose $B_H \in {\rm Disjoint}(\mathcal{B}_H) \cap {\rm HighGirth}_g(\mathcal{B}_H)$ for each $H$, take $B' = \bigcup B_H$, and verify the resulting projection treasury satisfies the required regularity (using $\Delta(B)$ bound to absorb edge deletions).

nodes.name: Full $B_0$-type Omni-Booster
nodes.statement: A quantum $K_q^r$-omni-booster $B$ with collection $(\mathcal{B}_H)$ is \emph{$B_0$-type} if every $\mathcal{B}_H$ is a copy of $B_0$ rooted at $H$. It is \emph{full} if for every $H \in \mathcal{H}$ and every $S \in \mathcal{S}(H)$ (the index set of possible rooted copies), $\mathcal{B}_H$ contains exactly one copy.

nodes.name: Random $p$-sparsification
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{B}_p := ((\mathcal{B}_H)_p : H \in \mathcal{H})$ where $(\mathcal{B}_H)_p$ is obtained by independently keeping each $B_H \in \mathcal{B}_H$ with probability $p$.

nodes.name: Random Quantum Booster — Intrinsic Properties
nodes.statement: For $q > r \ge 1$, $C \ge 1$, $g \ge 3$, $\alpha > 0$ and rooted $K_q^r$-booster $B_0$ of rooted girth $\ge g$, there exists $a_1$ such that for all $a \ge a_1$ there exists $n_1$: for $n \ge n_1$ and $(\alpha,g)$-regular $ga$-bounded $C$-refined sponge $(K_n^r, A, X, \mathcal{H})$ with $\mathcal{B} \in {\rm Full}_{B_0}$ and $p = \log^a n / \binom{n}{v(B_0)-q}$, with probability at least $0.9$ the sparsified $\mathcal{B}_p$ has $\Delta(\bigcup \mathcal{B}_p) \le a \Delta \log^a \Delta$ and ${\rm Disjoint}(\mathcal{B}_H) \cap {\rm HighGirth}_g(\mathcal{B}_H) \ne \emptyset$ for each $H$.
conclusions: with probability at least $0.9$, $\mathcal{B}_p$ has $\Delta(\bigcup \mathcal{B}_p) \le a \Delta \log^a \Delta$ and ${\rm Disjoint}(\mathcal{B}_H) \cap {\rm HighGirth}_g(\mathcal{B}_H) \ne \emptyset$ for each $H \in \mathcal{H}$

nodes.name: Random Quantum Booster — Extrinsic Properties
nodes.statement: For $q > r \ge 1$, $C \ge 1$, $g \ge 3$, $\alpha \in (0, \tfrac{1}{2(q-r)})$ and rooted $K_q^r$-booster $B_0$ of rooted girth $\ge g$, there exists $a_2$ such that for all $a \ge a_2$ there exists $n_2$: for $n \ge n_2$, $(\alpha,g)$-regular $ga$-bounded $C$-refined sponge $(K_n^r, A, X, \mathcal{H})$, $\mathcal{B} \in {\rm Full}_{B_0}$ and $p$ as above, with probability at least $0.9$, ${\rm Proj}_g(\mathcal{B}_p, A, K_n^r, X)$ is $(\binom{n}{q-r}, 2\alpha \binom{n}{q-r}, \frac{1}{4g(q-r)}, 2\alpha)$-regular.
conclusions: with probability at least $0.9$, ${\rm Proj}_g(\mathcal{B}_p, A, K_n^r, X)$ is $(\binom{n}{q-r}, 2\alpha \binom{n}{q-r}, \frac{1}{4g(q-r)}, 2\alpha)$-regular

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem HighGirthQuantumOmniBooster
nodes.statement: Set $a = \max(a_1, a_2)$, $n_0 = \max(n_1, n_2)$, $p = \log^a n / \binom{n}{v(B_0)-q}$. By Lemmas~\ref{lem:RandomQuantumIntrinsic} and~\ref{lem:RandomQuantumExtrinsic}, $\mathcal{B}_p$ satisfies (1) and (2) each with probability $\ge 0.9$, and the union bound supplies a $\mathcal{B}_p$ satisfying both.

nodes.name: $p$-vertex-random subhypergraph
nodes.statement: $H_p$ is the subgraph induced on a vertex set $X$ obtained by independently retaining each vertex of $H$ with probability $p$.

nodes.name: Kim-Vu Hypergraph Concentration
nodes.statement: For all integers $k \ge 1$ there exists $n_0$ such that for $p \in (0,1]$ and $n \ge n_0$: if $H$ is a $k$-uniform multi-hypergraph on at most $n$ vertices, $K > 0$ satisfies $p^i \ge \Delta_i(H)/K \cdot \log^{4k+2} n$ for all $i \in [k]$, and $e(H) \le K$, then $\Pr[e(H_p) \le p^k \cdot 2K] \ge 1 - n^{-\log n}$.
assumptions: $H$ is a $k$-uniform multi-hypergraph on at most $n$ vertices
conclusions: $\Pr[e(H_p) \le p^k \cdot 2K] \ge 1 - n^{-\log n}$

nodes.name: Boosters Containing a Set of Cliques
nodes.statement: For $q > r \ge 1$, $C \ge 1$, $g \ge 3$ and rooted $K_q^r$-booster $B_0$ of rooted girth $\ge g$, there exists $C'$ such that for any $C$-refined sponge $(G, A, X, \mathcal{H})$, $\mathcal{B} \in {\rm Full}_{B_0}$, $b = v(B_0) - q$ and edge $e$ or matching $Z$ of small size: $|\mathcal{B}(e)| \le C' \Delta n^{b-1}$, $|\mathcal{B}_{\rm small}(Z)| \le C' \frac{\Delta}{n} \binom{n}{b} n^{-(q-r)|Z| - \mathbf{1}_{|Z|\ge 2}}$, $|\mathcal{B}_{\rm large}(Z)| \le C' \binom{n}{b} n^{-(q-r)|Z|}$.
assumptions: edge $e \in G$ or ${\rm Girth}_{K_q^r}^g(G)$-avoiding matching $Z$ of $\mathcal{D}$ with $|Z| \le g-2$
conclusions: $|\mathcal{B}(e)| \le C' \Delta n^{b-1}$, $|\mathcal{B}_{\rm small}(Z)| \le C' (\Delta/n) \binom{n}{b} n^{-(q-r)|Z| - \mathbf{1}_{|Z|\ge 2}}$, $|\mathcal{B}_{\rm large}(Z)| \le C' \binom{n}{b} n^{-(q-r)|Z|}$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma BoostersContainingSetOfCliques
nodes.statement: Bound the number of $H \in \mathcal{H}$ containing a fixed face $F$ of given size by $C$-refinement; multiply by the number of remaining vertices in $V(B_0) \setminus V(H)$. Distinguish $|F| \le r-1$ and $|F| \ge r$ to recover (1) and (2). Apply rooted-girth lower bound on $v(Z)$ to convert vertex counts into the $(q-r)|Z|$ exponent.

nodes.name: $g$-booster-configuration
nodes.statement: An \emph{$g$-booster-configuration} of $\mathcal{B}$ is $\{U_1,\ldots,U_m\} \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ with $m \ge 2$, $|U \cap \mathcal{B}_H| \le 1$ for all $H$, such that $\exists F \in {\rm Girth}_{K_q^r}^g(G)$ partitioned into $F_1,\ldots,F_m$ with $F_i \subseteq (U_i)_{\rm on}$ or $F_i \subseteq (U_i)_{\rm off}$.

nodes.name: Girth-$g$ configuration hypergraph of $\mathcal{B}$
nodes.statement: ${\rm Girth}_g(\mathcal{B})$ has vertex set $\bigcup_{H \in \mathcal{H}} \mathcal{B}_H$ and edges precisely the $g$-booster-configurations of $\mathcal{B}$.

nodes.name: Large Intersect Bound
nodes.statement: For $q > r \ge 2$, $g \ge 3$, $Q \in V({\rm Girth}_{K_q^r}^g(K_n^r))$ and $J \subseteq K_n^r$: $|{\rm Large}_J(Q)^{(s)}| \le (sq) \binom{sq}{r-1} \binom{sq}{q}^s n^{(q-r)(s-1)} \frac{\Delta(J)}{n}$.
conclusions: $|{\rm Large}_J(Q)^{(s)}| \le (sq) \binom{sq}{r-1} \binom{sq}{q}^s n^{(q-r)(s-1)} \Delta(J)/n$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition LargeIntersect
nodes.statement: Order $V(F) \setminus V(Q)$ so that the last vertex lies in some $e \in J$; count choices of $m$, $v_1,\ldots,v_{m-1}$, $e$, $v_m$, and the chosen $q$-subsets.

nodes.name: Booster Configuration Counts ($\mathcal{B}^*$ bound)
nodes.statement: For $q > r \ge 1$, $C \ge 1$, $g \ge 3$, $B_0$ of rooted girth $\ge g$, there exists $C'$ such that for $C$-refined sponge $(G, A, X, \mathcal{H})$, $\mathcal{B} \in {\rm Full}_{B_0}$, ${\rm Girth}_{K_q^r}^g(G)$-avoiding matching $Z$ of $\mathcal{D}$, and $s, s', m$ with $s \ge |Z| \ge 1$, $1 \le m \le s'-s$: $|\mathcal{B}^*(Z, s', s, m)| \le C' \binom{n}{q-r}^{s-|Z|} \binom{n}{b}^m \cdot \frac{1}{n}$ if $|Z| \ge 2$, otherwise $\le C' \binom{n}{q-r}^{s-|Z|} \binom{n}{b}^m \cdot \frac{\Delta}{n}$.
assumptions: integers $s, s', m$ with $s \ge |Z| \ge 1$, $1 \le m \le s'-s$
conclusions: the stated $|\mathcal{B}^*(Z,s',s,m)|$ bounds (1) and (2) hold

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma GirthConfigPrelim
nodes.statement: Bound $|\mathcal{G}(Z)^{(s')}|$ via codegrees and Proposition~\ref{prop:LargeIntersect}; multiply by $|\mathcal{B}(F_i)|$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:BoostersContainingSetOfCliques}.

nodes.name: Girth Config Booster Degrees
nodes.statement: For $q > r \ge 1$, $C \ge 1$, $g \ge 3$, $B_0$ of rooted girth $\ge g$, there exists $C'$ such that for $C$-refined sponge and $\mathcal{B} \in {\rm Full}_{B_0}$: (1) $\Delta_{s,t}({\rm Girth}_g(\mathcal{B})) \le C' \binom{n}{b}^{s-t} \cdot \frac{1}{n}$ for $g \ge s > t \ge 2$; (2) $\Delta_{s,1}({\rm Girth}_g(\mathcal{B})) \le C' \binom{n}{b}^{s-1} \cdot \frac{\Delta}{n}$ for $g \ge s > 1$.
conclusions: $\Delta_{s,t}({\rm Girth}_g(\mathcal{B})) \le C' \binom{n}{b}^{s-t} \cdot \frac{1}{n}$ for $g \ge s > t \ge 2$ and $\Delta_{s,1}({\rm Girth}_g(\mathcal{B})) \le C' \binom{n}{b}^{s-1} \cdot \frac{\Delta}{n}$ for $g \ge s > 1$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma GirthConfigBoosterDegrees
nodes.statement: Sum $\mathcal{B}^*(Z, s', t', s-t)$ over relevant $t', s'$ via Lemma~\ref{lem:GirthConfigPrelim}, splitting on whether $t' \ge 2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma RandomQuantumIntrinsic
nodes.statement: Show four bad-event bounds (1)-(4) each fail with probability at most $0.01$; combine via union bound. Bounds (3) and (4) use Corollary~\ref{cor:KimVu} on auxiliary multi-hypergraphs encoding pairwise intersections and low-girth booster configurations.

nodes.name: Setup parameters and basic counts
nodes.statement: Choose $a$ large; set $b := v(B_0)-q$. Bound $\Delta(X \cup A) \le (C+1)\Delta \le (C+1) n/\log^{ga} n$, $|\mathcal{S}(H)| \in [\binom{n}{b}/2, \binom{n}{b}]$, $|\mathcal{H}| \le C^2 \Delta n^{r-1}$, and $n_0 \le n^{r+b}$.

nodes.name: Claim (1): $|(\mathcal{B}_H)_p| \ge \frac{1}{4} \log^a n$
nodes.statement: By linearity $\mathbb{E}[|(\mathcal{B}_H)_p|] \ge \frac{p}{2} \binom{n}{b} = \frac{\log^a n}{2}$. Apply the Chernoff bound and the union bound over $\mathcal{H}$.

nodes.name: Claim (2): $\Delta(\bigcup \mathcal{B}_p) \le a \Delta \log^a \Delta$
nodes.statement: Bound $\mathbb{E}[d_{B_1}(R)]$ via Lemma~\ref{lem:BoostersContainingSetOfCliques} and apply Chernoff for each $R \in \binom{V(K_n^r)}{r-1}$.

nodes.name: Claim (3): few non-disjoint boosters
nodes.statement: Construct an auxiliary 2-uniform $J$ encoding intersecting boosters; apply Corollary~\ref{cor:KimVu} with $K = \binom{n}{b}^2 / (24 \log^a n)$ to bound $e(J_p) \le \log^a n / 12$.

nodes.name: Claim (4): few low-girth boosters
nodes.statement: Build $J = \bigcup_{B_H \in \mathcal{B}_H} {\rm Girth}_g(\mathcal{B})(B_H)$; bound $\Delta_i(J^{(k)})$ via Lemma~\ref{lem:GirthConfigBoosterDegrees} and apply Corollary~\ref{cor:KimVu} for each $k \in \{2,\ldots,g-1\}$.

nodes.name: Conclude via union bound
nodes.statement: Combine claims (1)-(4); (1), (3), (4) imply ${\rm Disjoint}(\mathcal{B}_H) \cap {\rm HighGirth}_g(\mathcal{B}_H) \ne \emptyset$.

nodes.name: $g$-clique-booster-configuration
nodes.statement: Subset $U \subseteq {\rm Design}_{K_q^r}(G) \cup \mathcal{B}$ with $U' = U \cap {\rm Design}_{K_q^r}(G) \ne \emptyset$, $U \cap \mathcal{B} = \{U_1,\ldots,U_m\}$, $|U \cap \mathcal{B}_H| \le 1$, and $F \in {\rm Girth}_{K_q^r}^g(G)$ with $U' \subseteq F$ partitioned into $F_1,\ldots,F_m$ with $F_i \subseteq (U_i)_{\rm on}$ or $(U_i)_{\rm off}$.

nodes.name: Girth-$g$ extended configuration hypergraph ${\rm Extend}_g(\mathcal{B})$
nodes.statement: Vertex set $V({\rm Girth}_{K_q^r}^g(G)) \cup V({\rm Girth}_g(\mathcal{B}))$; edges are $g$-clique-booster-configurations. Bi-uniform decomposition by $(s_1, s_2)$ with corresponding bi-degree $\Delta_{(t_1,t_2)}$.

nodes.name: Extend Config Booster Degrees
nodes.statement: For $q > r \ge 1$, $C \ge 1$, $g \ge 3$, $B_0$ of rooted girth $\ge g$, there exists $C'$ such that: for $s_1 \ge t_1 \ge 0$, $s_2 \ge t_2 \ge 0$ with $s_1 + s_2 > t_1 + t_2 \ge 1$, (1) if $t_1 + t_2 \ge 2$ or $(s_1, t_1) = (1, 0)$, then $\Delta_{(t_1,t_2)}({\rm Extend}_g(\mathcal{B})^{(s_1,s_2)}) \le C' \binom{n}{q-r}^{s_1-t_1} \binom{n}{b}^{s_2-t_2} / n$; (2) otherwise the bound has $\Delta/n$ instead of $1/n$.
conclusions: the bi-degree bound holds with prefactor $1/n$ in case (1) and $\Delta/n$ otherwise

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma ExtendConfigBoosterDegrees
nodes.statement: Mirror Lemma~\ref{lem:GirthConfigBoosterDegrees} but track joint indices $(t_1, t_2)$; treat $t_1 + t_2' \ge 2$ and $t_1 + t_2 = 1$ separately.

nodes.name: Uncommon Degree Bound
nodes.statement: For $q > r \ge 1$, $C \ge 1$, $g \ge 3$, $B_0$ of rooted girth $\ge g$, there exists $C'$ such that for $C$-refined sponge, $\mathcal{B} \in {\rm Full}_{B_0}$, $Q \in V({\rm Girth}_{K_q^r}^g(G))$ and $v \notin V(Q)$ and integer $k \ge 1$: $|\{\mathcal{Z} \in {\rm Extend}_q(\mathcal{B})^{(2,k)}(Q) : v \in V(\mathcal{Z})\}| \le C' \binom{n}{q-r} \binom{n}{b}^k \cdot \frac{1}{n}$.
conclusions: $|\{\mathcal{Z} \in {\rm Extend}_q(\mathcal{B})^{(2,k)}(Q) : v \in V(\mathcal{Z})\}| \le C' \binom{n}{q-r} \binom{n}{b}^k / n$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma UncommonDegree
nodes.statement: Partition $\mathcal{F}$ into four classes $\mathcal{F}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{F}_4$ by where $v$ falls (in $V(F)$, in $V(B_{H_i}(S_i)) \setminus V(H_i)$, in $V(H_i)$ with small or large intersection) and bound each class.

nodes.name: Decompose tuple set $\mathcal{F}$
nodes.statement: Define $\mathcal{F}$ over $(F, F_0, (F_1,\ldots,F_k), (B_1,\ldots,B_k))$ with $v$-coverage; partition into $\mathcal{F}_1, \mathcal{F}_2, \mathcal{F}_3, \mathcal{F}_4$.

nodes.name: Bound $|\mathcal{F}_1|$
nodes.statement: When $v \in V(F)$, count $F$ with one fixed vertex; multiply by $|\mathcal{B}(F_1,\ldots,F_k)|$ via Lemma~\ref{lem:BoostersContainingSetOfCliques}.

nodes.name: Bound $|\mathcal{F}_2|$
nodes.statement: When $v$ falls into one $V(B_{H_i}(S_i)) \setminus V(H_i)$, count refined cliques saving a factor of $1/n$.

nodes.name: Bound $|\mathcal{F}_3|$
nodes.statement: When $v \in V(H_i)$ and $B_{H_i}(S_i) \in \mathcal{B}_{\rm small}(F_i)$, similar count using $C$-refinement.

nodes.name: Bound $|\mathcal{F}_4|$
nodes.statement: When $v \in V(H_i)$ and $B_{H_i}(S_i) \in \mathcal{B}_{\rm large}(F_i)$, count $F$ admitting a special edge $e \subseteq V(F)$ with $e \cup \{v\} \subseteq V(H)$.

nodes.name: Combine claims
nodes.statement: Sum the four bounds to obtain the lemma.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma RandomQuantumExtrinsic
nodes.statement: Show seven bad-event bounds (1)-(7) each hold with probability at least $0.99$; (1)-(3) bound vertex degrees in $G_1, G_2, H$; (4) is deterministic; (5)-(7) bound various codegrees of $H$ by applying Corollary~\ref{cor:KimVu} to auxiliary multi-hypergraphs built from ${\rm Extend}_g(\mathcal{B})$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:UncommonDegree}.

nodes.name: Setup parameters and notation
nodes.statement: Set $b = v(B_0) - q$, $D = \binom{n}{q-r}$, $\beta = \frac{1}{2g(q-r)}$, $\mathcal{D}, \mathcal{R}, \mathcal{G}$ as in proof. Bound $\Delta(X \cup A)$, $|\mathcal{S}(H)|$, $|\mathcal{H}|$.

nodes.name: Claim (1): degree of $v$ in $G_1$ at least $(1-2\alpha) D$
nodes.statement: Build $J = \bigcup_{Q \in \mathcal{D}: v \in Q} \bigcup_{k} \{Z \setminus Q\}$; apply Corollary~\ref{cor:KimVu} for each $k$.

nodes.name: Claim (2): degree of $v$ in $G_2$ at least $D^{1-2\alpha}$
nodes.statement: Analogous construction over $\mathcal{R}$; argue separately for $i \in [k-1]$ and $i = k$, leveraging $D/n \le D^{1-1/(q-r)}$.

nodes.name: Claim (3): $\Delta(H^{(j)}) \le 2\alpha D^{j-1} \log D$
nodes.statement: Construct $J$ for fixed $e$ and $j \in \{2,\ldots,g-1\}$; bound and apply Corollary~\ref{cor:KimVu}.

nodes.name: Claim (4): codegree bound on $G_1 \cup G_2$ holds always
nodes.statement: Use the original treasury regularity and inclusion $G_i \subseteq$ corresponding parts of the unprojected design/reserve.

nodes.name: Claim (5): $\Delta_t(H^{(s)}) \le D^{s-t-\beta/2}$
nodes.statement: Build $J = \bigcup_k \{Z \setminus V(\mathcal{G})\}$ for $Q \in \mathcal{Q}_t$; apply Corollary~\ref{cor:KimVu}.

nodes.name: Claim (6): max 2-codegree of $G_1 \cup G_2$ with $H$
nodes.statement: Construct $J$ over $Q \in V(\mathcal{G})$ with $v \in Q$; apply Corollary~\ref{cor:KimVu} on each $J^{(k)}$.

nodes.name: Claim (7): max common 2-degree of $H$
nodes.statement: Construct $J$ over $f \in V(\mathcal{G})$ and pairs $(Z_1, Z_2)$ for $e_1, e_2$; bound $e(J^{(k)})$ via Lemmas~\ref{lem:ExtendConfigBoosterDegrees} and~\ref{lem:UncommonDegree}; apply Corollary~\ref{cor:KimVu}.

nodes.name: Combine via union bound
nodes.statement: Union bound across claims (1)-(7) yields ${\rm Proj}_g(B, A, K_n^r, X)$ regular with the target parameters with probability at least $0.9$.

nodes.name: Erdos cogirth configuration
nodes.statement: A \emph{$(w_1, w_2)$-cogirth-$g$-configuration} of $G$ is $(\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2)$ where each $\mathcal{B}_i$ is a $K_q^r$-packing of girth $\ge g$ and $\mathcal{B}_1 \cup \mathcal{B}_2$ contains a $(i(q-r)+r-1, i)$-configuration for some $2 \le i \le g-1$. The Erdos version excludes proper sub-cogirth-configurations.

nodes.name: Cogirth Configuration Hypergraph ${\rm Cogirth}_{K_q^r}^g(G)$
nodes.statement: Configuration hypergraph $H$ on $E(\mathcal{D}_1) \cup E(\mathcal{D}_2)$ whose edges are the $(w_1,w_2)$-cogirth-$g$-Erdos-configurations.

nodes.name: Cogirth Configuration Degree Bound
nodes.statement: For all $q > r \ge 1$, $g \ge 3$, there exists $C \ge 1$ such that for all $n$ and $1 \le t < s \le g$: $\Delta_t({\rm Cogirth}_{K_q^r}^g(K_n^r)^{(s)}) \le C \binom{n}{q-r}^{s-t} / n$.
conclusions: $\Delta_t({\rm Cogirth}_{K_q^r}^g(K_n^r)^{(s)}) \le C \binom{n}{q-r}^{s-t} / n$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition CogirthDegrees
nodes.statement: Bound $|\mathcal{C}^{(s)}(U)|$ by counting unions of two packings achieving girth and codegree constraints.

nodes.name: Cogirth-$g$ design treasury ${\rm CoTreasury}_q^g$
nodes.statement: Two-copy version of the design treasury, joining $\mathcal{D}_i, \mathcal{R}_i, \mathcal{G}_i$ for $i \in \{1,2\}$ together with the cogirth configuration hypergraph $\mathcal{C}$.

nodes.name: Collective cogirth of two omni-absorbers
nodes.statement: Two omni-absorbers $A_1, A_2$ for $X$ have \emph{collective cogirth at least $g$} if each individually has collective girth $\ge g$ and for every pair $L_1, L_2$ of $K_q^r$-divisible subgraphs, $\mathcal{Q}_{A_1}(L_1)$ and $\mathcal{Q}_{A_2}(L_2)$ have cogirth at least $g$.

nodes.name: Cogirth-$g$ projection treasury of two omni-absorbers
nodes.statement: ${\rm CoProj}_g(A_1, A_2, G, X) := {\rm CoTreasury}_q^g(G, G \setminus A_1, G \setminus A_2, X) \perp \mathcal{M}(A_1, A_2)$ where $\mathcal{M}(A_1, A_2) = \{M_1 \cup M_2 : M_1 \in \mathcal{M}(A_1), M_2 \in \mathcal{M}(A_2)\}$.

nodes.name: High Cogirth Omni-Absorber Theorem
nodes.statement: For all $q > r \ge 1$, $g \ge 3$ and $\alpha \in (0, \tfrac{1}{2(q-r)})$, there exist $a, n_0$ such that for $n \ge n_0$: assuming Theorem~\ref{thm:HighCogirthBooster} for $r-1$, if $X \subseteq K_n^r$ with $\Delta(X) \le n / \log^{ga} n$ and ${\rm CoTreasury}_q^g(K_n^r, K_n^r, X)$ regular, then there exist two $K_q^r$-omni-absorbers $A_1, A_2$ with $\Delta(A_i) \le a \Delta \log^a \Delta$ and collective cogirth $\ge g$, plus a $(\binom{n}{q-r}, 4\alpha \binom{n}{q-r}, \frac{1}{8g(q-r)}, 3\alpha)$-regular subtreasury of ${\rm CoProj}_g(A_1, A_2, K_n^r, X)$.
assumptions: $X \subseteq K_n^r$ with $\Delta(X) \le n/\log^{ga} n$ and ${\rm CoTreasury}_q^g(K_n^r, K_n^r, X)$ is regular
conclusions: two $K_q^r$-omni-absorbers $A_1, A_2$ exist with bounded $\Delta$, collective cogirth $\ge g$, and a regular subtreasury of ${\rm CoProj}_g(A_1, A_2, K_n^r, X)$

nodes.name: High Cogirth Omni-Booster Theorem
nodes.statement: For all $q > r \ge 1$, $C \ge 1$, $g \ge 3$ and $\alpha \in (0, \tfrac{1}{2(q-r)})$, there exist $a, n_0$ such that for $n \ge n_0$: assuming Theorem~\ref{thm:HighCogirthBooster} for $r-1$, if $(K_n^r, A, X)$ is an $(\alpha, g)$-regular $ga$-bounded $C$-refined sponge, then there exist two $K_q^r$-omni-boosters $B_1, B_2$ for $A$ and $X$ with $\Delta(B_i) \le a \Delta \log^a \Delta$, collective cogirth $\ge g$, and a $(\binom{n}{q-r}, 4\alpha \binom{n}{q-r}, \frac{1}{8g(q-r)}, 3\alpha)$-regular subtreasury of ${\rm CoProj}_g(B_1, B_2, A, G, X)$.
conclusions: two $K_q^r$-omni-boosters $B_1, B_2$ for $A$ and $X$ exist with the stated bounded $\Delta$, collective cogirth $\ge g$, and a regular subtreasury of ${\rm CoProj}_g(B_1, B_2, A, G, X)$

nodes.name: High Cogirth Quantum Omni-Booster Theorem
nodes.statement: For all $q > r \ge 1$, $C \ge 1$, $g \ge 3$ and $\alpha \in (0, \tfrac{1}{2(q-r)})$, there exist $a, n_0$ such that for $n \ge n_0$: assuming Theorem~\ref{thm:HighCogirthBooster} for $r-1$, if $(K_n^r, A, X, \mathcal{H})$ is an $(\alpha, g)$-regular $ga$-bounded $C$-refined sponge, then two quantum $K_q^r$-omni-boosters $B_1, B_2$ exist with (1) ${\rm Disjoint}(\mathcal{B}_{i,H}) \cap {\rm HighGirth}_g(\mathcal{B}_{i,H}) \cap {\rm HighCogirth}_g(\mathcal{B}_{i,H}) \ne \emptyset$ for each $H, i$ and (2) ${\rm Proj}_g(B_1, B_2, A, K_n^r, X)$ is $(\binom{n}{q-r}, 3\alpha \binom{n}{q-r}, \frac{1}{4g(q-r)}, 3\alpha)$-regular.
conclusions: two quantum $K_q^r$-omni-boosters $B_1, B_2$ exist with the stated Disjoint $\cap$ HighGirth $\cap$ HighCogirth condition (1) and projection-regularity (2)

nodes.name: Cogirth booster configuration hypergraph ${\rm Cogirth}_g(\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2)$
nodes.statement: Vertex set $\bigcup_{H \in \mathcal{H}} \mathcal{B}_{i,H}$; edges are $g$-cogirth-booster-configurations of $\mathcal{B}_1 \cup \mathcal{B}_2$ (paired across two disjoint copies of $G$).

nodes.name: Cogirth Config Booster Degrees
nodes.statement: For $q > r \ge 1$, $C \ge 1$, $g \ge 3$, $B_0$ of rooted girth $\ge g$, there exists $C'$ such that for $C$-refined sponge and pair $\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2$ of copies of $\mathcal{B} \in {\rm Full}_{B_0}$: $\Delta_t({\rm Cogirth}_g(\mathcal{B})^{(s)}) \le C' \binom{n}{b}^{s-t} / n$ for all $2g \ge s > t \ge 1$.
conclusions: $\Delta_t({\rm Cogirth}_g(\mathcal{B})^{(s)}) \le C' \binom{n}{b}^{s-t} / n$

nodes.name: CoExtend Config Booster Degrees
nodes.statement: For $q > r \ge 1$, $C \ge 1$, $g \ge 3$, $B_0$ of rooted girth $\ge g$, there exists $C'$ such that for $C$-refined sponge and pair $\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2$ of copies of $\mathcal{B} \in {\rm Full}_{B_0}$: $\Delta_{(t_1, t_2)}({\rm CoExtend}_g(\mathcal{B})^{(s_1, s_2)}) \le C' \binom{n}{q-r}^{s_1-t_1} \binom{n}{b}^{s_2-t_2} / n$ for $s_1 \ge t_1 \ge 0$, $s_2 \ge t_2 \ge 0$, $s_1 + s_2 > t_1 + t_2 \ge 1$.
conclusions: $\Delta_{(t_1,t_2)}({\rm CoExtend}_g(\mathcal{B})^{(s_1,s_2)}) \le C' \binom{n}{q-r}^{s_1-t_1} \binom{n}{b}^{s_2-t_2} / n$

nodes.name: Existence of High Girth Designs — Minimum Degree Version
nodes.statement: For all integers $q > r \ge 2$ and every integer $g \ge 2$, there exist $n_0$ and $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for all $K_q^r$-divisible $r$-uniform hypergraphs $G$ with $v(G) \ge n_0$ and $\delta(G) \ge (1 - \varepsilon) v(G)$, there exists a $K_q^r$-decomposition of $G$ with girth at least $g$.
conclusions: $G$ admits a $K_q^r$-decomposition of girth at least $g$

nodes.name: Sharp minimum degree threshold for high girth $K_q$-decompositions
nodes.statement: What is the best possible minimum degree threshold for Theorem~\ref{thm:HighGirthMinDegree}; in particular when $r=2$, can it match the best known bounds for $K_q$-decompositions of graphs of high minimum degree?

nodes.name: High girth Steiner systems in random hypergraphs
nodes.statement: Do threshold results for the existence of Steiner systems in $G(n,p)$ and in the $q$-uniform random binomial hypergraph (Delcourt-Kelly-Postle DKPIII, DKPIV) extend to high girth Steiner systems?
